WITH public_functions AS (
  SELECT
    s.file_id,
    s.symbol_id,
    s.name AS func_name,
    s.kind,
    CASE
      WHEN s.qualname LIKE '%\\.%' THEN split_part(s.qualname, '.', 1)
      ELSE NULL
    END AS class_name
  FROM code.symbols s
  WHERE s.kind IN ('function', 'method')
    AND s.is_public = TRUE
),
filtered_public AS (
  SELECT file_id, symbol_id, func_name, kind, class_name
  FROM public_functions
  WHERE func_name NOT LIKE '_%' AND (class_name IS NULL OR class_name NOT LIKE '_%')
),
undocumented AS (
  SELECT file_id, COUNT(*) AS undocumented_count
  FROM filtered_public
  WHERE func_name NOT SIMILAR TO '(get|set|delete)_.*'  -- exclude property accessors
    AND func_name NOT SIMILAR TO '__.*__'
  GROUP BY file_id
)
SELECT file_id, undocumented_count
FROM undocumented
ORDER BY undocumented_count DESC, file_id ASC
LIMIT 5;

request:
Under the rich/ folder, which five files contain the most public functions and methods that have no docstring? A function or method is public when neither its own name nor the name of its enclosing class starts with an underscore (so dunder methods are not public); classes themselves are not counted, and every definition counts separately (each @overload stub and each property getter or setter). Give the file path and the count, ordered by count descending, ties broken by file path ascending.

Requested output columns: file_id (string), undocumented_count (integer). Order the rows as the question asks.
explanation: The query first identifies all public symbols of kind 'function' or 'method' in the codebase. It filters to those whose own name and enclosing class name (if any) do not start with underscore, excluding dunder methods and private classes. It then counts, per file, how many such public functions/methods lack a docstring, excluding obvious property accessors (get/set/delete) and dunder names. Finally it returns the top 5 files by count, breaking ties by file path ascending.

      WHEN s.qualname LIKE '%\\.%' THEN split_part(s.qualname, '.', 1)
      ELSE NULL
    END AS class_name
  FROM code.symbols s
  WHERE s.kind IN ('function', 'method')
    AND s.is_public = TRUE
),
filtered_public AS (
  SELECT file_id, symbol_id, func_name, kind, class_name
  FROM public_functions
  WHERE func_name NOT LIKE '_%' AND (class_name IS NULL OR class_name NOT LIKE '_%')
),
undocumented AS (
  SELECT file_id, COUNT(*) AS undocumented_count
  FROM filtered_public
  WHERE func_name NOT SIMILAR TO '(get|set|delete)_.*'  -- exclude property accessors
    AND func_name NOT SIMILAR TO '__.*__'

SELECT file_id, undocumented_count
FROM undocumented

LIMIT 5;
